His autem sic se habentibus, et in omnibus antiquis et probatissimis et veteribus scripturis numero hoc posito, et testimonium perhibentibus his, qui facie ad faciem Johannem viderunt, et ratione docente nos, quoniam numerus nominis bestiz secundum Greecorum computationem per literas quee in eo sunt, sexcentos — habebit, et sexaginta, et sex; hoc est, decadas sequales hecatontasin, et hecatontadas eequales monasin ; Numerus enim qui digitus sex, similiter custoditus, recapitulationes ostendit universee apostasize ejus que initio, et que in mediis temporibus, et quae in fine erit ; ignoro quomodo erraverunt quidam sequentes idiotismum, et medium frustrantes numerum nominis, quinquaginta numeros deducentes, pro sex decadis unam decadem volentes esse. [ Hoc autem arbitror scriptorum peccatum fuisse, ut solet fieri, quoniam et- per literas numeri ponuntur, facile literam Graecam, que Sexaginta enuntiat numerum, in iota Grecorum literam expansam ;]| post deinde quidam sine exquisitione hoc acceperunt; alii quidem simpliciter et idiotice usurpaverunt denarium numerum : quidam autem per ignorantiam ausi sunt et nomina exquirere, habentia falsum erroris numerum. Sed his quidem qui simpliciter et malitia hoe fecerunt, arbitramur veniam daria Deo. Quotquot autem secundum inanem gloriam statuunt nomina continentia falsum numerum, et quod a se fuerit adinventum nomen, definierunt esse illius qui venturus est; non sine damno tales exient, quippe qui et semetipsos, et credentes sibi seduxerunt. Et priquidem damnum est excidere a veritate, et quod non sit, quasi arbitrari: post deinde, apponenti vel auferenti de Scriptura peenam non modicam fore, in quam incidere necesse est eum qui sit talis, Subsequetur autem et aliud non quodlibet periculum eos, qui falso preesumunt scire nomen ejus. Si enim aliud quidem thi putant, aliud autem ille habens adveniet, facile seducentur ab eo, quasi necdum adsit ille, quem cavere convenit. 2. thought_title: The Number of the Beast's Name
pass_a_gloss: These things being so, and the number being established in all ancient and approved and old scriptures, and the testimony being borne by those who saw John face to face, and reason teaching us that the number of the name of the beast, according to the computation of the Greeks through the letters which are in it, is six hundred and sixty-six, that is, equal tens of hundreds and equal hundreds of units; for the number which is six, similarly preserved, shows the recapitulations of his apostasy, which is from the beginning, and which is in the middle times, and which will be in the end; I do not know how some have erred, following foolishness, and frustrating the middle of the number of the name, deducing fifty numbers, wishing one decade to be instead of six decades. But I think this was a sin of the writers, as often happens, because they also put numbers through letters; easily, the Greek letter which announces the number sixty, was expanded into the iota of the Greeks; afterwards, some accepted this without investigation; others, indeed, used the number ten simply and foolishly; some, however, dared to investigate names, having the false number of error. But to those who did this simply and with malice, we think pardon will be given by God. As many, however, as establish names containing the false number, and what was invented by themselves, defining it to be the name of the one who will come, will not exit without loss, since they have deceived themselves and those who believe in them. And indeed, the loss is to fall away from the truth, and to think that what is not, is; afterwards, to add to or take away from Scripture will bring no small penalty, which it is necessary for one such as this to incur. But another danger, not insignificant, will also follow those who falsely presume to know his name. For if they think one thing, but he comes having another, they will easily be seduced by him, as if he were not yet present, whom it is fitting to beware of. Therefore, it is necessary for such people to learn and return to the truth of the number of the name; so that they may not be considered among the false prophets. But knowing the firm number announced by Scripture, that is, six hundred sixty-six, let them first endure the division of the kingdom into ten; afterwards, when those are reigning, and beginning to correct their affairs, and increase their kingdom, the one who will come unexpectedly, claiming the kingdom for himself, and terrifying the aforementioned, having the name containing the aforementioned number, let them truly recognize him to be the abomination of desolation. The Apostle also says this: When they will say, Peace and security, then sudden destruction will come upon them. But the prophet has revealed not only his sudden coming, but also the tribe of six by which he will come, saying: The voice of the neighing of his horses will stir up the whole earth; and he will come and devour the earth and its fullness, and the city, and those who dwell in it. And because of this, this tribe is not counted among those who are saved in the Apocalypse. It is therefore more certain and without danger to hold to the fulfillment of prophecy, than to suspect and divine any names; since many names can be found having the aforementioned number, and nevertheless, the same question will remain. For if many names are found having this number, which he who comes will bear, it is asked: Because we do not say these things on account of a lack of names having the number of his name, but on account of fear and zeal for the truth: For the name Teitan has the number about which it is asked, but we affirm nothing about it. The name has the number six hundred sixty-six; and it is very likely, since this is the last kingdom, and the Latins are those who now reign; but we do not glory in this. And also the name Titan, written with two Greek vowels e and i, has the predicted number in itself, and is worthy of faith. The number of its letters is six, with single syllables consisting of three letters, and it is old and removed; for none of the kings who are according to us have been called Titan, nor do the idols which are publicly worshiped among the Greeks and barbarians have this name. And this name is considered divine by many, so that even the sun is called Titan by those who now hold it; and it contains a certain show of vengeance and punishment, because he pretends to avenge those who have been evilly treated. And this name is also ancient, and worthy of faith, and royal, but more tyrannical. When, therefore, this name Titan has so much persuasion, and so much likelihood, that we gather from many things that perhaps the one who will come will be called Titan; we, however, will not endanger ourselves in this, nor will we assert and declare that he will have this name; knowing that if it were necessary to proclaim his name openly at the present time, it would have been proclaimed by him who also saw the Apocalypse. For it was not seen long before, but almost in our own century, at the end of Domitian's reign. Now, however, the number of the name shows that we should beware of the one who will come, knowing who he is; but the name itself is silent, because it is not worthy to be proclaimed by the Holy Spirit. For if it had been proclaimed by him, perhaps it would have remained for a long time. But now, since it is not, and it will ascend from the abyss, and go into perdition, as if it were not; so also his name has not been proclaimed; for the name of what is not is not proclaimed. But when the Antichrist will have established all things in this world, he will reign for three years and six months, and will sit in the temple of Jerusalem; then the Lord will come from heaven in the clouds, in the glory of the Father, sending him, indeed, and those who obey him, into the lake of fire; but bringing the times of the kingdom to the just, that is, rest, sanctifying the seventh day; and restoring the promise of inheritance to Abraham; in which kingdom the Lord says that many will come from the east and the west, and will recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
